habitat: Singly or in pairs in marshes and the vegetation around inland waters, especially sewage ponds. It walks on mudflats and reed-bed fringes and can swim.
summary: A common resident on Newman’s African Swamphen page. Large and bulky, purple-blue and dark green. The bill and frontal shield are entirely red and the legs are pink. It is larger than Allen’s Gallinule. The immature is duller and brownish, with red-brown legs. The call is a deep explosive bubbling, varied with shrieks and groans. Newman’s page uses Porphyrio madagascariensis. This list keeps Porphyrio porphyrio and the English name Purple Swamphen. The Kemp name Purple Gallinule and the code NB were left unchanged.

similar.note: Allen’s Gallinule is smaller, with a shield that is not entirely red. African Swamphen has a red shield and bill and pink legs.

research.note: Newman calls African Swamphen a common resident, and Avibase lists Porphyrio madagascariensis without marking it rare, so all twelve months are listed. This list keeps the name Porphyrio porphyrio. The grade A call is from Cape Town and the filename records a narrow filter. The Kruger photograph is distant. The Kemp name Purple Gallinule and the code NB were left unchanged.
